metadata.summary: Luke Humphries was not punished for a raft of missed finishing doubles as he beat a below-par Dave Chisnall to reach the second round of the World Grand Prix in Leicester.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade reach round two as Josh Rock and Chris Dobey dumped out | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries and James Wade reach round two as Josh Rock and Chris Dobey dumped out Luke Humphries - the new title favourite after Luke Littler's exit - beats below-par Dave Chisnall before appearing to shush member of crowd, will face Jermaine Wattimena next; other winners on Tuesday include Gian van Veen, Gary Anderson, Stephen Bunting and debutant Niels Zonneveld Wednesday 30 September 2026 00:02, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries taunted a fan who seemingly agitated the former world champion following his World Grand Prix win over Dave Chisnall Luke Humphries was not punished for a raft of missed finishing doubles as he beat a below-par Dave Chisnall to reach the second round of the World Grand Prix in Leicester. Humphries - who has made the last three finals in this event, winning in 2023 ahead of two runners-up finishes since - is the new favourite to triumph this year following defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night. Cool Hand, sporting a scab on his forehead he put down to an allergic reaction, defeated Chisnall 2-0 while averaging only 80.41 and going at 26 per cent on his doubles as he secured a second-round meeting with Chris Dobey's conqueror Jermaine Wattimena. metadata.summary: Luke Humphries says he must improve if he is to challenge for a second World Grand Prix title and admits he would have preferred defending champion Luke Littler to have avoided an early exit.
metadata.content: World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries 'hates' added title pressure from Luke Littler's shock early exit in Leicester | Darts News | Sky Sports Skip to main content World Grand Prix Darts: Luke Humphries 'hates' added title pressure from Luke Littler's shock early exit in Leicester Luke Humphries is now favourite to win the World Grand Prix title after Luke Littler's early exit to Luke Woodhouse; Humphries discussed the added pressure he faces after a first-round win over Dave Chisnall he labelled 'one of the worst performances' he has played Wednesday 30 September 2026 06:51, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries taunted a fan who seemingly agitated the former world champion following his World Grand Prix win over Dave Chisnall Luke Humphries says he must improve if he is to challenge for a second World Grand Prix title and admits he would have preferred defending champion Luke Littler to have avoided an early exit. Humphries - the 2023 champion and a runner-up the last two editions of the double-start major - produced a lacklustre performance during his straight-sets victory over Dave Chisnall at the Mattioli Arena. The world No 2 hit under 27 per cent of his checkout attempts and averaged 80.41, his lowest in the tournament since 2022, although was relieved to avoid joining Littler and Michael van Gerwen in being beaten in the first round. messages.text: Buttler: McCullum can go 'all in' on Cricket World Cup without Test role

metadata.summary: Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter.
metadata.content: Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances | Cricket News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Joss Buttler says Brendon McCullum's removal as England Test coach may have boosted Cricket World Cup chances Brendon McCullum left his role as England Test coach in July; Jos Buttler believes the move has allowed the New Zealander to focus solely on helping England win the Cricket World Cup; Buttler has been ruled out of the upcoming Pakistan white-ball tour due to injury Tuesday 29 September 2026 15:39, UK Image: Jos Buttler says Brendon McCullum (pictured) is 'all in' on helping England win the Cricket World Cup in 2027 Jos Buttler believes Brendon McCullum's removal as Test coach may have boosted England's World Cup chances, with the New Zealander now "all in" on lifting the trophy next winter. McCullum was relieved of his red-ball duties in July , with Stephen Fleming eventually named as his successor , but remained in charge of a limited-overs set-up that ended the summer with a record of 11 wins and two defeats. That included ODI series wins over India and Sri Lanka , raising England's stock in a format that has seen them decline since they became world champions in 2019.
